messages.subject: Starter plan pricing - analysis and proposal
messages.body:
Quick recap:

1. We have been at €49/month for Starter since launch. Our costs per account (support load, infrastructure, scan processing) have risen roughly 18% over two years.
2. I analysed churn against the willingness-to-pay survey we ran in November and against the competitor set (RouteBee charges €55 for a weaker feature set). Starter customers showed the lowest price elasticity of any tier - the tier is used daily for dispatch, which makes switching costly.
3. Proposal: raise Starter from €49 to €59/month. The attached table models three options (no change, €55, €59) against expected churn and revenue; €59 wins even at the pessimistic churn assumption. Approximate uplift at current account mix is €9-11k/month gross.
4. If we agree, I need 4 weeks of notice to customers, so an effective date of 1 March works. Existing customers question: see the table's column C, we need a call on grandfathering.

Thanks!
Priya

messages.subject: RE: Starter plan pricing - analysis and proposal
messages.body:
Hola,

I have to push back here 🚨 140 of our 310 accounts are on Starter. That is nearly half our customer base getting a 20% increase in one letter. My pipeline for Q1-Q2 is full of exactly this segment - small couriers comparing us against RouteBee on price, and RouteBee is at €55.

I am not against a rise, but €49 to €59 in one step gives every competitor I am fighting a free talking point. Could we phase it, or at least look at €55? I would rather win the renewal conversation than explain a 20% jump on a €49 product.

Saludos,
Tomás

messages.subject: RE: Starter plan pricing - analysis and proposal
messages.body:
Dear all,

I have reviewed Priya's model and I support the €59 proposal. The cost-per-account figures she cites match the finance view, and the churn assumptions in the pessimistic scenario are, if anything, conservative - I would gently suggest we are underweighting the daily-usage stickiness of the dispatch workflow. The incremental revenue of roughly €9-11k per month at the current mix is material relative to our run-rate, particularly with the hosting and payments cost items on this year's agenda.

On Tomás's €55 alternative: it leaves approximately €4k per month on the table and, in my view, does not meaningfully soften the competitive message he is worried about - a 12% increase is still an increase a competitor can quote.

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
Chief Financial Officer, Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: Starter plan pricing - analysis and proposal
messages.body:
Hi all!

From a messaging angle: a price increase is actually a super opportunity to re-launch the value story for Starter! I would frame it as "new capabilities, new price" and time the announcement with a feature highlight campaign. If we do 1 March, I would want the comms ready by 1 February to give customers a proper 4-week notice window, aligned with what Priya said.

One caution though - if we do this AND make other big changes (billing, hosting) in the same quarter, customers will feel nickel-and-dimed. Happy to put a one-pager together!

Excited about this,
Chloe

messages.subject: RE: Starter plan pricing - analysis and proposal
messages.body:
Quick recap of where we are:

1. Proposal on the table: €49 → €59, effective 1 March, 4 weeks notice.
2. Open question flagged in my original email: what happens to the 140 existing Starter accounts - full increase, grandfathering, or something in between. That changes the revenue maths materially and I would not want to decide it in the same breath as the headline price.
3. Tomás's concern noted; Helen's counter noted.

Marta - could you give a steer on the headline number today? The notice window for 1 March closes next week, after which we are into April.

Thanks!
Priya

messages.body:
€59, 1 march. tomás, send me the competitor math if it's real and we'll talk about the existing accounts separately.

M
